title: Protein-protein interaction prediction via structure-based deep learning
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) play an essential role in life activities. Many machine learning algorithms based on protein sequence information have been developed to predict PPIs. However, these models have difficulty dealing with various sequence lengths and suffer from low generalization and prediction accuracy. In this study, we proposed a novel end-to-end deep learning framework, RSPPI, combining Residual Neural Network (ResNet) and Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), to predict PPIs based on the protein sequence physicochemistry properties and spatial structural information. In the RSPPI model, ResNet was employed to extract the structural and physicochemical information from the protein 3D structure and primary sequence; the SPP layer was used to transform feature maps to a single vector and avoid the fixed-length requirement. The RSPPI model possessed excellent cross-species performance and outperformed several state-of-the-art methods based either on protein sequence or gene ontology in most evaluation metrics. The RSPPI model provides a novel strategic direction to develop an AI PPI prediction algorithm.
